1:<!-- The design sketch for the first reserved fork of PLAN.md, the array representation on the compile path, written 2026-09-19 by a worker for Pavol and revised the same day after his three rulings (§6 quotes them): unboxed double[] is decided, the sized types are built as the team designed them with the checker taught nat parameters, and library work copies the library's own patterns. It assembles what next-climb.md §3a said a sketch must hold, adds the nat plan the second fork needs, and ends in a decision tree for what is still open. Eight probe programs were compiled in a private cache (§9); no tracked file was changed. Every recommendation is labelled "default" and decides nothing. One line per paragraph. -->
27:Storage is one object per rank-1 array, holding boxed values. `PrimitiveArray[\T, nat s0\]` (`LibraryBuiltin/NativeArray.fss:15-27`) binds `get`, `put` and `init0` to Java glue; the glue allocates an `AtomicArray` of the evaluator's boxed `FValue`s (`interpreter/glue/prim/PrimitiveArray.java:35, 44-56`; `evaluator/transactions/AtomicArray.java:23`). A rank-2 array is a rank-1 array with the index folded as `i s1 + j`, row by row (`__DefaultArray2`, `FortressLibrary.fss:2415-2421`); rank 3 the same. So the interpreter's arrays are already flat, row-major storage under a trait; what they are not is unboxed. One exception exists and nothing uses it: `PrimImmutableRR64Array[\nat s0\]` over a Java `double[]` (`NativeArray.fss:41-51`; `glue/prim/PrimImmutableRR64Array.java:40`), referenced by no library file.
79:What is built: the interpreter's trait layer, `Indexed`, `ReadableArray`, `Array[\E,I\]`, `Array1[\T, nat b0, nat s0\]`, `Vector`, `Matrix`, `Array3`, with `fill`, `map`, `ivmap`, `t()` and the views written in Fortress as they are in `FortressLibrary.fss`; beneath them, in the place of `PrimitiveArray[\T, nat s0\]` (`__DefaultVector`'s `mem` field, `.fss:2204-2205`), one hand-written native store per element type: the `double[]` class of (b) for `RR64`, `FZZ32Vector` for `ZZ32`, a boxed `Object[]` store for every other `T`. The checker sees the library's own types; the model's `Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]`, `Vector[\RR64,s\]`, `Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]` resolve as written.
83:How a hand-written class sits under a stamped generic trait: `FZZ32Vector extends fortress.CompilerBuiltin.ZZ32Vector.DefaultTraitMethods implements ZZ32Vector` (`FZZ32Vector.java:16-17`), a non-generic Fortress trait whose generated abstract class the Java extends. So the store's trait must be non-generic (`RR64Store`), declared in Fortress as extending the generic `Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]`, and the generated abstract class then carries the stamped supertype. Unprobed: that a non-generic trait extending an instantiated generic supertype with a hand-written implementation class compiles and links; it is the first thing the array rung of §8 finds out.
101:The drafts say nothing about arrays. `Library/incomplete/` (24 files) contains no mention of an array. `Library/GeneratorLibrary.fss` and `.fsi` (783 lines, imported by nothing) are the generator and reduction protocol, `Container`, `DefaultGeneratorImplementation`, without `Indexed` or any array. `Fortress.Operators.fsi.INCOMPLETE` is the algebra above `Number` and names no aggregate. What the team shipped in this world is `ZZ32Vector`, and it is the only precedent with code behind it.
133:Storing objects and views passing nats up: `__DefaultVector[\T, nat s0\]() extends Vector[\T,s0\]` with `mem: PrimitiveArray[\T,s0\]` (`:2204-2205`), `__DefaultArray2` (`:2415`), `__DefaultMatrix` (`:2563`), `__DefaultArray3` (`:2780`), `TransposedArray2` (`:2425`), `TransposedMatrix[\T, nat s0, nat s1\](mem: Matrix[\T,s1,s0\])` (`:2571`), `SubArray2/3` (`:2451, 2798`), `Row`, `Col` (`:2473, 2484`), `PrimitiveArray[\T, nat s0\]` (`NativeArray.fss:18`).
149:What the loader must do with a nat argument beyond what it does: supply a value for a nat in value position inside a template. Either the instantiater rewrites the `getstatic <Component>$n.ONLY` reference into a constant when it stamps `⟦…,5,…⟧` (an instruction-level substitution in `Instantiater`, the job the expando stub at `InstantiatingClassloader.java:168-172` was left for), or the code generator emits a read from the run-time type descriptor, which today refuses `IntArg` (`CodeGen.java:5783`). Under the two-place representation the library's value uses of a nat are few (`i s1 + j` in `__DefaultArray2`, the `N[\s0\]` witness in `subarray`) and the store's field can serve the first; the second is explicit-only. So the value mechanism is a `.java` rung of its own, needed for the full port and not for the first kernels. Default: the field first, the name-to-constant substitution when the port reaches `subarray`.
151:Run-time sizes: `array[\RR64\](n)` with `n` computed cannot name its class at compile time. Either a native helper builds the stamped name from the integer and asks the loader for `Array1⟦FRR64,0,4192⟧` by that string, which is a string from a number and unprobed, or the run-time-sized factory returns the unsized `Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]` as it already does in the model (`FlatArrays.fss:14-17`) and only literal and symbol sizes get sized classes. Default: the second; it is what the model writes today, and the `reflect` group of §6c is then the one library pattern the compiled world does not reproduce until the first is probed.
157:The shadow route (`next-climb.md:102-104`; the recipe of `perf-probes/template-check/run-all.sh`): copies of the five files compiled with `scala.tools.nsc.Main` into `shadow-classes`, placed first on the class path; the gate can be run with the shadow overlaid on `ProjectFortress/build`, as the template fix was (its 31 lines went green that way, `33-testfast.out`, `34-testsystem.out`). What it buys: the two unknowns, the object crash's source and the export checker's reach, are found without a sealed-tree edit, and the design of the inference variable can be tried as a reserved-name `IntRef` (the plan's option B) before the AST node (option A) is added, which a shadow cannot do because the AST is regenerated by `ant compileAll`. What it costs: a second toolchain path per iteration, and a prototype that differs from the real edit in that one representation. Assessment: the tree is unsealed and the batch script already runs `.scala` rungs under the full gate with the test written first, so the shadow is not a gate substitute; it is worth one worker session for the two unknowns and nothing more. Default: one shadow session for the object crash and the export checker, then the rung in the tree with option A.
165:Question 4, where sizes live: closed by Pavol, in the type as the team designed. Consequences: the checker rung of §6e precedes the first sized declaration; the export checker and the object crash are on the path, not optional; every distinct size is a stamped class; the run-time-sized factory returns the unsized `Array` until the string-from-number route is probed (§6d, default).
168:Branch "native stores per element type under the library's generic objects": `__DefaultVector[\T, nat s0\]` keeps its shape and its `mem` field is the `RR64` store for `RR64`, `FZZ32Vector` for `ZZ32`, the boxed store otherwise, chosen by the factory from the run-time type tag; the interpreter's own layering with `PrimitiveArray` replaced; one unprobed link, the non-generic store trait under the generic `Array` (§4c).
170:Default: the first; it needs one probe and no loader change, and it is the library's own structure.
